# NOTES ON THE FIVE BOOKS (for later Q&A; text itself not needed)

## BOOK 1 — *Emmanuel Appadocca; or, Blighted Life: A Tale of the Boucaneers* (Maxwell Philip, 1854, 2 vols; Vol I ch. I–XV, Vol II ch. XVI–XXXI)

**Setting/premise:** Gulf of Paria, Trinidad, Venezuela coast. Preface: author’s indignation at US slave-holders treating slave-children cruelly; Trinidad his native isle; dedicated to Harry Daniels, Esq.

**Characters:** Emmanuel Appadocca (pirate captain; mixed-blood, quadroon-looking, ~25, learned, stoic, cynical, misanthrope; “Scorpion” password); Lorenzo (chief officer, Carmonte descendant, loves Agnes, real name St. James Carmonte); Sebastian (watch officer); Jim Splice (old English sailor, scar on forehead, gossip); Jack Jimmy (grotesque little Black servant of the master fisherman, speaks Creole English, “Garamighty”); master fisherman (mulatto Spanish, unnamed); Gregoire (officer); Bembo (black boy attendant); Agnes (beautiful captive, daughter of a planter; guardian a priest); James Willmington (Appadocca’s father, cowardly cracker-selfish planter; abandoned son, refused bread); Charles Hamilton (Commander’s son, officer, Appadocca’s friend from Paris university); the commander (old, gouty-ish, honest, “Hum”); Feliciana (Venezuelan Ranchero’s daughter, falls in love, later mad); Ranchero/Batt-like characters; Llaneros Juancito; Domingo, Gustave, Baptiste, Alphonso, Jose, Pedro; Lorenzo ’s men; Gustave; mail; Ti-O? (no).

**Plot, in order:** Fishing boat captured by pirate schooner (Black Schooner, “Scorpion”, death’s-head flag) in Gulf of Paria; Jack Jimmy blanketed and toe burned; prize ship *Letitia* of Bristol (Capt. ?) seized after fight; father Willmington recognizes Appadocca, is put on a cask (with biscuits) and cast adrift; priest and Agnes are landed at Granada in cutter; Lorenzo writes love letter to Agnes; pirate duel over share of dead Francis (liar killed; cannonball-tied drowned); Willmington rescued by sloop, reports to St Thomas; Appadocca arrested at St Thomas by British man-of-war (commander, son Charles); Appadocca sends Hamilton letter; attempted rescue by Lorenzo fails (shark); pirate schooner disguised as brig/brigantine; Jack Jimmy watches; Appadocca escapes by clay pitcher, jaguar, rescued by Llaneros/Feliciana; Feliciana pleads; Appadocca leaves; hurricane wrecks schooner on Trinidad (Chaguaramas-like bay), Appadocca on sunken rock; Jack Jimmy buries him; Feliciana mad at grave (Vol II end: she visits Mother Celeste sorceress; Feliciana later “Succouring Mother”). Lorenzo marries Agnes, plantation retreat. Willmington later accused by Appadocca’s ghost; ends in Boston? (no—Willmington dies in torture-cask and cabin).

**Key quoted lines:** “Garamighty!”; “Scorpion”; “I never change”; “Men of such boldness…”

---

## BOOK 2 — *Shadowed by a Detective; or, The Woman in Wax* (René de Pont-Jest, trans. Virginia Champlin; Magnet Detective Library No. 106; detective William Dow)

**Characters:** Ada Ricard (ex-Mrs. James Gobson; real name Anna Bell, twin of Kitty Bell); Willie Saunders (fat cracker-merchant, lover); Mary (maid); Colonel Edward Forster (kidnapper-lover, yacht *Gleam*); Fat Kelly (police chief); Captain Young (detective, giant); William Dow (retired Philadelphia doctor, detective, alias Clement Murray); Miss Jane (16, his adopted ward); Mrs. Wandright (governess); Robertson Jr. (agency head, Robertson Bros & Co.); James Gobson (brutal husband); Albert Busby? no; Sheriff Mortimer; coroner Davis; Mr. Macready (lawyer); O’Brien (DA); Judge Douglas; Meyer (hangman); Rev. Midler; Toby Tew? no; Kitty Bell (Mrs. Gobson second, impostor); Harris Burnett; Mrs. Busby? (no); John Butler (trapper); Jimin (Sioux chief, Swift Deer); Washah, Winka, Makeni; Captain Semmas (Fort Dakota); Mole? no.

**Plot:** Kidnapping at Ada’s ball (17 East 23rd St, NYC, 1865, Indian masks). Forster carries her by yacht to Staten Island; Saunders hires Robertson agency; collision in fog; Ada’s body found at Wharf 43/32 by sailors (Toby’s tar barrel); Bellevue morgue; Albert Moor (sculptor) makes wax head; Dow’s deduction; Gobson arrested; trial, condemned, reprieve (Meyer breaks leg); Kitty Bell (impostor) reveals; Gobson re-marries Ada; Dow stages trap at Jamaica Plain villa (Kitty as “Ada” in wax); Gobson attacks wax; arrested; drowns (Blackwell’s Island), body under Wharf 32. Kitty Bell sentenced to a year; later Paris.

---

## BOOK 3 — *The Ghost of Mystery Airport* (Van Powell; Saalfield 1932)

**Characters:** Garry (Garfield) Duncan (15, student pilot, cool); Chick (Chickering Brown, 13, impulsive, timid then brave); Don McLeod (17, pilot, nephew of airport manager Bruce McLeod); Scott (test pilot, “Great Scott”, likes spooks; secret villain/ghost); Doc Morgan (handyman, herbs, drinks); Vance (control chief, initials J.V., John Vance); Toby Tew (theatre-owner, boatman); John Tioga (Indian son), Ti-O-Ga (old medicine man); Smith (mail flyer, impostor); Chubby (assistant); Henry (mechanician); police chief.

**Plot:** Ghost seen in clouds every seventh night; airplanes “collide”; Dragonfly (three-seat biplane), Dart (red two-seater); mail plane crash; tracing of brigantine camouflaged as airplane; helicopter “Demon” (Man Who Never Lived); Chick finds Doc; Indian charm pouch with three Palace Theatre passes; film projected onto smoke; Don flies mail from ship *Caledonia*; treasure chart of pirate brig *Lady O’ Fortune* in Devil’s Sinkhole; Scott (disguised) is culprit; tear-gas; Scott’s plane crashes on shore. Ends “And thus the Ghost of Mystery Airport passed.”

---

## BOOK 4 — *Love and the Ironmonger: A Plain Tale of Upper Thames Street* (F. J. Randall, 1908)

**Characters:** George Early (junior clerk, ironmonger, blackmailer/schemer); Fairbrother & Co. (iron firm, Upper Thames St.); Old Joseph Fairbrother (dies; 3 legacies £500/yr each for reform); Thomas Parrott (head clerk, mean; later bride Lucy Perkins, milliner); Albert Busby (cashier, liar, wife Fanny, Clapham; sister-in-law tale); James “Jimmy” Gray (accountant, drinker; wife Emily/Em, Leytonstone, lodger George); Ellen Fairbrother (heiress; from Australia; cousin “Tops”, = Ellen daughter of John Fairbrother with strawberry mark; Aunt Phoebe); Mrs. Haskins (landlady, Walworth); Mrs. Carey; Mole (detective, Dibbs & Dubbs lawyers; Tommy Morgan whisky); Caroli (mesmerist); Cattermole (chemist, friend); Billy Budd, Cacklin (junior clerks); Mrs. Early (Ellen); Aunt Phoebe; Canon? no.

**Plot:** Legacies conditional on reform; George borrows from each; reveals secrets; reversion to George; Gray & Busby conspiracy; chaperoned by Aunt Phoebe; Caroli hypnosis; train chase; fire-trick in cloakroom; tree fall; fake twin in Hastings inn; Cannon Street meeting cousin; “Name o’ Phoebe”; Brixton house.

---

## BOOK 5 — *The Spring Song* (Forrest Reid, 1916, Edward Arnold)

**Characters:** Griffith “Grif” Weston (13, sensitive, sleepwalker, dog Pouncer, bulldog); Jim (9); Ann (10, plump, reddish hair, freckles); Barbara (12); Edward (15, vain); Palmer Dorset (15, red hair, brown eyes, detective-minded, friend of Edward; revolver from Doctor O’Neill); Aunt Caroline (sister? father’s sister, Canon Annesley’s daughter); Canon Annesley (grandfather, writes on fairies); Miss Johnson (governess, novel *Be True, Fond Heart*); Mr. Drummond (curate); Clement Bradley (organist, real name Tennant, insane, killed brother-type? “pushed brother off bridge”); Captain Narcissus Batt, Miss Nancy, Miss Jane Batt (Batts, house by pond); Billy Tremaine (dead grandson, flute, Spring Song by Gian Peruzzi); Doctor O’Neill; Robert (coachman); Johnnie (boy); Bridget, Hannah (servants); Pan & Syrinx (cats); George (burglar, Prairie Dick, circus rider).

**Plot:** Arrival at Glebe, Ballinreagh (Ireland), June; croquet tournament; play *Be True, Fond Heart* parody; Grif hears flute, walks in sleep; lunches at Batts; Bradley’s ghost story; Pouncer stolen by circus man George; Grif runs off after circus, sleeps out; Palmer and Edward ambush burglar George with shot; church burns, Bradley leaps from tower; Grif’s illness, Miss Nancy’s comforting; autumn; school plans. Ends with Grif asleep in Miss Nancy’s arms.
